overall: At just after 1 AM ET, Atlanta is sitting at 73.4°F with zero velocity — temperatures have been flat and are essentially at the overnight minimum. The very high dewpoint of 69.8°F (near 90% relative humidity) signals a deeply moist airmass, which typically suppresses daytime heating by promoting cloud cover and limiting surface insolation. The day has not yet begun to warm, so the running max of 73.4°F will need significant afternoon heating to reach model-forecast levels.
forecast_obs_notes: Model guidance is in moderate disagreement: GFS and HRRR are bullish at 85.0°F, while ECMWF pulls back to 83.1°F and NBM — which blends multiple models and accounts for local climatology — comes in lowest at 82.3°F. The spread of ~2.7°F across the four models reflects real uncertainty, and the NBM's lower projection often performs well in high-moisture regimes where convective cloud development can cap afternoon highs.
max_temp_prediction: The more confident ensemble signal (odd model, Tier 2 at 22%) points to an 81–82°F ceiling, which aligns closely with the NBM and ECMWF guidance and is consistent with the moisture-limiting factor from the high dewpoint. The GFS/HRRR 85°F scenario requires drier, sunnier conditions that the current dewpoint and NBM suggest are unlikely. Best estimate is approximately 82.5°F, with moderate confidence — the moist airmass is the key downside driver, and any early cloud breaks could push temps toward 83–84°F.
